**Why the model gave you a low‑risk rating**  
The model looks at a few key pieces of your credit profile. First, your revolving‑credit utilization is very low (about 4 % of the available balance). Using only a small portion of your credit limits signals that you manage debt responsibly, and this pulls your risk down. Second, the model sees that you are 42 years old. In this particular calculation, being older adds a small amount of risk, which is why it nudges the score up a little. Finally, you have four open credit lines and loans. Having several active accounts shows a longer credit history and spreads risk, which again lowers the overall chance of default. When these factors are combined, the model estimates a 16 % probability of default and classifies you as “low risk.”

**What you can do next**  
The system did not find any specific, feasible actions that would reliably change the decision. Continuing the habits that are already helping—keeping your credit‑card balances low and maintaining your existing credit accounts—will keep your profile strong. If you ever open new credit responsibly, the same low‑utilization pattern will continue to work in your favor.
